item.title: Health & Safety Manager
item.description: Location: London or Leeds Role Overview The Health & Safety Manager is a senior strategic role in the Bank’s central Health and Safety Function, acting as the second line of defence for governance, standards, expertise and assurance. The role owns the Health & Safety Management System, setting the governance framework, standards and assurance model, and ensuring it remains effective, robust and aligned with best practice, including ISO 45001 principles. You will design and maintain strong safety governance arrangements that enable first-line business areas to manage operational health and safety risks, supported by expert oversight, consistent standards and independent enterprise-level assurance. Working closely with the Head of Health & Safety and senior stakeholders, you will provide clear insight on risk exposure, control effectiveness and safety performance, helping executive leaders make informed decisions on health and safety risk. This is a governance, assurance and continuous improvement role, distinct from day-to-day operational safety delivery. It works in partnership with the Health and Safety Operations Support Lead, who supports operational coordination and compliance tracking. Together, these roles provide both first-line operational enablement and second-line oversight, helping the Bank operate an integrated, effective health and safety management system that reduces risk and supports proactive safety management across the organisation. Key Responsibilities Health and Safety Governance: Lead the development and continual improvement of the Bank’s health and safety governance framework and Safety Management System, aligned to ISO 45001, regulation and best practice. Standards, Policy and Documentation: Own the health and safety standards library and management system documentation, ensuring clear, current, risk-based guidance, procedures and evidence are maintained and audit-ready. Risk, Control and Assurance: Establish and maintain assurance over health and safety risks, test critical controls, challenge first-line risk management, escalate material issues and drive sustainable improvements. Reporting, Insight and Continuous Improvement: Provide clear, data-led reporting on risk, compliance, controls, audits and emerging issues, translating information into practical insight and improvement action. Stakeholder Engagement: Work with operational leaders, facilities, projects, suppliers, risk and audit teams to embed health and safety requirements, provide expert advice and constructive challenge. Leadership: Provide technical direction to colleagues and support a credible, high-performing function focused on effective governance, assurance and continuous improvement. Role Requirements What we’re looking for Minimum Criteria Demonstrable experience in health and safety, risk, assurance or governance within a complex or regulated organisation. Working knowledge of UK health and safety legislation, regulations and recognised standards. Experience producing clear reports, guidance or recommendations for managers or senior stakeholders. Essential Criteria Proven experience designing, improving or managing health and safety management systems, governance frameworks, standards, policies or procedures. Practical understanding of ISO 45001 principles and how these can be applied in a large organisation. Experience identifying material risks, maintaining risk registers, mapping assurance activity or assessing control effectiveness. Strong communication and influencing skills, with evidence of translating technical, regulatory or risk information into clear, decision-ready outputs. Experience leading or influencing improvement initiatives, audits or assurance activity that have strengthened health and safety performance, governance or culture. Desirable Criteria Chartered membership, professional certification or formal qualification in health and safety, risk, audit, governance or assurance. Experience in financial services, public sector, critical national infrastructure or another highly regulated environment. Experience supporting external certification, audits, regulatory reviews or assurance assessments. Experience using digital tools, dashboards or data analysis to improve risk visibility, action tracking, assurance or evidence management. The role reports to the Head of Health and Safety. It sits within the Health and Safety Function’s standards, assurance and risk visibility resource, and works closely with other specialists to support the wider Health and Safety Function team objectives. Location and Working Arrangements This role can be based at the organisation’s headquarters in London (Threadneedle Street) or the Leeds office. Regular travel between sites may be required to oversee commercial and performance activities across the UK portfolio. Flexible and hybrid working arrangements are supported, with a minimum expected on-site presence of 50% (approximately 3 days per week). All necessary IT equipment will be provided, and scheduling flexibility is offered to accommodate business and personal needs. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information This role offers a salary range in circa. Leeds: £62,480 - £70,290 and London: £69,440 - £78,120 based on skills and experience. Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . item.title: Health & Safety Operations Support Manager
item.description: Location: London or Leeds Role Overview Join the Bank's Health & Safety Function in a key role supporting the effective delivery of health and safety across a complex, high-profile organisation. As Health & Safety Operations Support Lead, you will help ensure our systems, data, controls and operational processes enable safe, compliant and consistent ways of working across the Bank. This is an excellent opportunity for a health and safety professional who enjoys combining operational delivery, systems oversight, compliance coordination and stakeholder engagement. You will play a central role in supporting statutory compliance, improving data quality, strengthening assurance activity and helping the Function move towards more proactive, evidence-led risk management. Working closely with the Head of Health & Safety, you will act as an important link between the central Health & Safety Function and stakeholders across the organisation, including first-line business units, property and facilities teams, second-line Risk colleagues and third-party suppliers. You will help ensure health and safety processes are implemented smoothly, compliance obligations are met, and the Bank’s safety management system operates effectively in practice. The role works alongside the Health & Safety Governance & Management Lead, with a shared focus on strong controls, clear assurance and continuous improvement. Together, these roles support an integrated approach to health and safety management, combining operational enablement with governance and assurance to reduce risk and promote proactive safety management across the organisation. What you’ll be doing Operational support and coordination: act as a key coordinator between the Health & Safety Function and first-line teams, helping clarify responsibilities, embed health and safety requirements into day-to-day operations, and support effective controls and initiatives. Systems administration and data quality: manage and maintain health and safety information systems, including incident reporting, risk assessment and compliance tracking tools, ensuring accurate records and reliable data for performance monitoring and reporting. Compliance coordination and assurance support: coordinate and track health and safety compliance and control activities, supporting statutory and regulatory obligations across areas such as asbestos, fire safety, electrical and gas safety, lifts, pressure systems and workplace hazard controls. Performance monitoring and risk visibility: gather and analyse health and safety metrics, compliance data and audit findings, producing clear reporting on key indicators such as risk assessment completion, statutory compliance, incident trends and training compliance. Continuous improvement and insight: use data, compliance intelligence and stakeholder feedback to identify trends, emerging risks and opportunities to improve health and safety processes, controls and ways of working. Stakeholder engagement and collaboration: build effective relationships with operational teams, property services and external suppliers, supporting clear communication of health and safety requirements and helping foster a consistent, collaborative safety culture across the Bank. About the team You will be part of the Health & Safety Function’s operational delivery resource and report to the Head of Health & Safety. Working closely with other specialists, you will help ensure the Function runs smoothly and delivers high-quality support, assurance and continuous improvement across the organisation. Role Requirements What we’re looking for Minimum criteria Health and safety experience: proven experience in health and safety operations or compliance within a complex or highly regulated environment, with broad understanding of statutory compliance, workplace health and safety practices and risk management principles. Systems and data capability: experience using health and safety management systems, preferably aligned to ISO 45001, with strong data management skills and the ability to maintain accurate, reliable records. Assurance and compliance knowledge: sound knowledge of health and safety legislation and regulatory requirements, with experience tracking compliance actions, supporting assurance activity and producing structured performance reports. Essential criteria Communication and stakeholder engagement: excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with operational teams, managers and external providers, and to communicate health and safety guidance clearly and confidently. Organisation and analysis: strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities, alongside the analytical capability to interpret safety data, identify trends and present clear, actionable insights. Desirable experience and qualifications Professional accreditation: a relevant health and safety qualification or certification, with a Level 6 Diploma or equivalent as a minimum. Sector knowledge: familiarity with banking, financial services or public sector environments, particularly where health and safety is managed across multiple locations and complex compliance requirements. Management systems and improvement: experience maintaining or improving health and safety management systems, particularly in line with ISO 45001 and the Plan-Do-Check-Act model, including involvement in audits, risk management or continuous improvement activity. Digital and data interest: an interest in using technology, analytics or digital tools to improve health and safety insight, compliance tracking and operational efficiency. Location and Working Arrangements This role can be based at the organisation’s headquarters in London (Threadneedle Street) or the Leeds office. Regular travel between sites may be required to oversee commercial and performance activities across the UK portfolio. Flexible and hybrid working arrangements are supported, with a minimum expected on-site presence of 50% (approximately 3 days per week). All necessary IT equipment will be provided, and scheduling flexibility is offered to accommodate business and personal needs. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. item.title: Non-Executive Directors
item.description: The National Audit Office (NAO) occupies a unique place in public life. As Parliament's independent public spending watchdog, we help hold government to account, support better financial management and highlight where public services can deliver better value and outcomes. As two non-executive directors reach the end of their terms, we are seeking two successors who will bring independent judgement, constructive challenge and strategic insight to the Board. This is a significant time to join the NAO. Our work reaches across the full breadth of government and public services, informing parliamentary scrutiny, promoting stronger financial management and highlighting innovation across the public sector. One appointee will bring recent and relevant audit practice experience, together with a strong understanding of audit quality, assurance and professional standards. They will be expected to chair the NAO's Audit and Risk Assurance Committee. The second will bring senior leadership experience from the Civil Service or wider public sector, with a deep understanding of government, public service delivery and leading complex organisations at scale. We are looking for exceptional individuals with board-level experience, sound judgement, political awareness and a strong commitment to public service. Successful candidates will help shape the NAO's strategic direction, contribute to its effective governance and provide independent challenge and oversight as part of an open, constructive and collaborative Board. This is an opportunity to contribute to one of the UK's most respected public institutions and to help shape the effectiveness, accountability and value of public services. It is essential that the NAO upholds the highest standards of propriety in its governance. To avoid any conflicts of interest, we are unable to consider applications from individuals who hold executive or non-executive positions within organisations audited by the NAO. Appointments are made by Parliament's Public Accounts Commission on the recommendation of the NAO Chair. Appointments are for a three-year term, renewable for a final three-year term. The recruitment process will include a pre-appointment hearing with the Public Accounts Commission. Saxton Bampfylde Ltd is acting as an employment agency advisor to the National Audit Office on these appointments. For further information about the role, including details about how to apply, please visit roles.saxbam.com using reference OAJXI. Alternatively email maria.dodson@saxbam.com. Applications should be received by noon on Monday 28 th September 2026.

item.title: Building Engineering Manager in Maint & Eng - Debden
item.description: Location: Debden, Essex. The Bank of England is the UK's central bank; our mission is to deliver monetary and financial stability for the British people. The Bank of England is a diverse organisation with each of its 4,000+ people are committed to public service and dedicated to promoting the good of the people of the United Kingdom by supporting monetary and financial stability. Department Overview The role of the banks Property department through its Operations and Maintenance Engineering team, is to maintain, enhance and support the occupied building environment, and to provide excellent engineering services for all Bank staff. In addition to maintaining and supporting the Bank’s primary business function, The Property team has responsibility for significant annual capital investment, supports business continuity, strategic health & safety management, internal & external events, general building facilities (switchboard, help desk and reception), catering, cleaning, post services and travel team whilst ensuring value for money is achieved in all Bank wide procurements. The Property department’s overall mission is to maintain, enhance and protect the Bank’s building environment including its engineering systems and to provide resilient services to maintain business as usual functionality. The Engineering team comprises <56 FTE and covers the Bank’s (x3) core properties located in London & Debden (Essex). The London properties, comprise of (x2) properties; the Banks grade 1 listed Head Office at Threadneedle St and a more traditional modern office building at 20 Moorgate. Our property located at Debden is the Banks print works. All (x3) buildings are highly critical to the Banks operations and possess various levels of critical systems to support those operations. Job Description The Building Engineering Manager is responsible for the safe, compliant and resilient operation of the building’s engineering systems and services at the Bank of England’s Debden site. The role provides operational leadership across engineering and building services that are essential to business continuity, ensuring the building environment is reliable, well maintained and enables occupants and users to work safely, comfortably and effectively at all times. The role also has responsibility for the end‑to‑end delivery of minor works and small capital replacement projects, ensuring they are appropriately scoped, safely delivered, and integrated with business‑as‑usual operations. Responsibilities The scope of services to be provided are as follows but are not exhaustive. Provide team leadership, operational assurance and strategic oversight of all building engineering systems, ensuring 24/7 resilience, compliance and performance within a complex, occupied and business-critical environment. Lead, develop and manage a multi-skilled team of maintenance, fabric technicians and apprentices, including performance management, capability development and succession planning. Ensure building services (including environmental comfort, lighting, power, water, life safety and support services) operate reliably and predictably to support business productivity, staff wellbeing and effective use of the building. Embed a high-performing culture focused on safety, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement. Provide operational oversight and assurance of building engineering systems to ensure continuous availability and resilience. Own the planning, prioritisation and assurance of planned maintenance activities across all building engineering systems, ensuring tasks are delivered safely, on time and to the required quality standard. Act as primary building systems engineering responsible person assuring 24/7/365 business functions. Accountable for system availability, reliability and recovery performance across all critical building services. Implementation of the Banks SSoW processes for employees and contractors. Act as the engineering lead during incidents, coordinating response, recovery and stakeholder communication to minimise business impact. Provide leadership and assurance for Safe Systems of Work (SSoW), risk assessments and permit-controlled activities for staff and contractors. Act as a visible health & safety leader, promoting a strong safety culture and compliance mindset across all activities. Own budgets and lead supplier performance, ensuring value for money, risk management and continuous improvement across all engineering contracts. Contribute to asset lifecycle planning, critical risk mitigation and medium-term engineering strategy for the Debden site. Use asset and maintenance data to identify trends, manage risk, inform prioritisation and support evidence-based decision-making. Produce and present monthly performance and assurance reports on planned and reactive maintenance, asset condition, compliance status and operational risk, providing clear insight to senior stakeholders. Support energy efficiency, plant optimisation and sustainability initiatives, working with specialist teams as required. Act as a Senior Authorised Person (HV/LV and/or mechanical), providing technical authority and assurance within defined Safe Systems of Work. Contribute to asset lifecycle planning, critical risk mitigation and medium‑term engineering strategy for the London site, including the identification and delivery of minor works and small capital interventions. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Engineering qualification (minimum HNC or equivalent) in a relevant discipline (e.g. electrical or mechanical engineering). Working knowledge of Safe Systems of Work (SSoW), including experience applying electrical and/or mechanical permit systems. Experience operating within a building services or engineering environment, supporting maintenance or operational activities. Essential Criteria Engineering operations and maintenance leadership – Previous experience leading engineering operations or maintenance teams, managing planned and reactive maintenance, and maintaining service performance across critical building systems. Compliance, risk, and safety management – Experience applying Safe Systems of Work, managing risk assessments and contractor controls, and maintaining compliance with health and safety requirements in an operational environment. System reliability and incident management – Experience maintaining system availability and resilience, including leading incident response, coordinating service recovery, and implementing actions to reduce operational risk. Commercial and supplier management - Demonstrable capability in budget management, supplier or contract oversight, cost control, and achieving value for money. Data, reporting and stakeholder management – Proven ability to use asset or maintenance data to support decisions, produce performance reporting, and present clear insight to senior stakeholders. Desirable Criteria Chartered or Incorporated Engineer status, or demonstrable progress toward professional registration with a relevant institution such as CIBSE, IET or IMechE. NEBOSH General Certificate or another recognised health and safety qualification. Experience using CAFM or similar maintenance management systems to manage assets, maintenance activity and reporting. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. For most roles where work can be carried out at home, we aim for colleagues to spend half of their time in the office, with a minimum of 40% per month. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them, their team and stakeholders. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. item.title: Scale E Agent in North West Agency, 23-month opportunity
item.description: Location: Manchester The Bank of England Agency Network The Bank’s Agents are the representatives of the Bank of England in the twelve Agencies across the English regions and Devolved Nations. The Agencies are the ‘eyes, ears and voice’ of the Bank in their respective parts of the United Kingdom. Agents play a crucial role in informing the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) and the Financial Policy Committee’s (FPC) assessment of the economic and financial environment through gathering, analysing, and reporting economic intelligence from regular meetings with their network of contacts. Agents talk to senior contacts from a wide range of organisations – from small businesses to large global companies – across all sectors of the economy, to gain an insight into how businesses are operating and their future plans. This provides a unique perspective into how the real economy is evolving and the factors driving those developments. The Agents also communicate policymakers’ core messages to business contacts and other local audiences across the UK. This includes regular presentations on the Monetary Policy Report and Financial Stability Report to support a widespread understanding and trust of the monetary and financial policy framework. Agents also coordinate interactions and host meetings between policymakers and their local contacts, so that they can hear the views of businesses and communities first-hand. Job Description Carries out external engagement within The North West of England and, on occasion, across the North East and Yorkshire and the Humber with the principal aim of gathering intelligence and carrying out representational functions for the key policy functions of the Bank of England. Works as part of a team on a technical Area of Expertise (AoE), led by a Technical Agent, to construct an economic narrative and/or strategy, contributing to policy analysis, discussion and decision making. The Area of Expertise for this role, which may change over time, will be employment, pay and capacity utilisation. Agents, as part of their AoE team, analyse and summarise qualitative intelligence to bring an ongoing, timely narrative to the policy discussion. Agents as part of a rota can lead the analysis and present to the MPC during a policy round with the support of the lead Technical Agent and AoE team. Agents work on specific projects assigned to Working Groups and may lead on specific projects and matrix manage other members of the Working Group. Agents will work closely with the Senior Data Scientist and the Data team to trial and implement new tools and analytical approaches. Scale E Agents can expect to undertake rotating secondments to other parts of the Bank or work on structured joint analytical projects, to broaden their knowledge, expertise and networks in the Bank. Reports to: The scale D Managing Agent for the North of England (currently Alex Golledge) Location: Needs to live in, or very close to, the North West region. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Experience in summarising qualitative information into reports for use by decision makers Experience in communicating effectively with senior business people An understanding of and interest in economics and/or economic policy Essential criteria: Demonstrate an understanding of the Bank’s approach to monetary policy and its policy framework more generally. A good communicator, comfortable interacting with senior external contacts. Ability to learn quickly, work independently and deliver good quality outputs to agreed timetables. Able to work collaboratively with colleagues within and/or outside the Bank. Desirable criteria: Experience of conducting interviews to gather qualitative data. Experience of delivering presentations to diverse audiences and explaining complex messages clearly and concisely. A full driving licence. A degree in economics or equivalent work experience Travel is an essential part of the role. A car allowance and mileage payment are paid to the role holder to facilitate this. This role requires a combination of in-person meetings and virtual meetings with Agency contacts in the North West and, occasionally, elsewhere in the North of England. It also requires regular in-person meetings with the Agency team in Manchester and with the other teams in the North of England in Leeds. There are also occasional meetings with UK-wide colleagues in London and Leeds. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. The salary range for this role is, Manchester: £72,720 - £81,810. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. item.title: Head of Workplace and Estates
item.description: The FCA has retained Odgers to look after this role on our behalf. The following link will take you to the Odgers website where you will be able to apply www.odgers.com/96619 About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator ; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth , by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime , focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. The Role The FCA has a workforce of 5,500 spread across three sites in London, Edinburgh, and Leeds. London is the largest office with approximately 4,800 staff located in 12 Endeavour Square. We have committed to continued growth outside of London and have also adopted hybrid working practices. There is a small in-house team with the majority of services outsourced under two key contracts. The team sits within the Operations Division and the Finance & Corporate Services Directorate, reporting to the Director of Finance. This role will lead the team, oversee our contracts, and ensure the FCA is getting maximum value from its estate. The building and services are key to our staff and our employment offer and maintaining a high level of excellence is key. There are also opportunities to evolve the offering as hybrid working practices become clearer, technologies advance and our ways of working change. What will the candidate get from the role? Providing strategic direction and leadership for a team of Facilities, Estates, Security and H&S professionals in relatively new buildings. Managing a significant budget and contractual relationships Opportunity to develop and evolve space in line with changing working practices Be part of an organisation that plays a significant part in protecting consumers and our economy Key responsibilities: Lead the team with overall responsibility for Estates, Facilities, Corporate Security and Health & Safety. This includes all aspects of setting overall direction, objectives and measuring performance and key trends. The facilities being overseen include front of house, security, cleaning, gym, staff restaurant and AV. Management of the relationships with both our superior landlord and a significant tenant that the FCA subleases to. Overseeing key suppliers who deliver our services to ensure compliance, value and the highest quality of service. Ensuring the estate is resilient, has adequate contingency plans and running disaster recovery responses where necessary Ensuring the organisation has the right space design and planning to continue effectively meeting its objectives . Ensuring our estate delivers against our sustainability goals. Developing and delivering a long-term strategy for the department , aligning to broader divisional and organisational strategies Leading on performance, capability, and culture within the department , with a strong focus on operational excellence Building a strong and inclusive directorate that attracts and develop diverse talent. Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Strong experience of managing a facilities, estates, and infrastructure team Strong leadership capabilities - a role model for the Estates & Facilities team with the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams through change. Extensive experience of managing outsourced Facilities Management supplier contracts Experience of estate planning, space planning and running projects Essential Extensive experience of managing a facilities operation in a corporate workplace Experience of managing relationships with both landlord and managing significant tenants Strong experience of health & safety management Strong experience of physical security risk assessment and management Responsibility for keeping leased building in operation and maintaining its condition Ability to get the best out of suppliers working in partnership with others across the FCA Confident, assertive and able to influence and challenge stakeholders Desirable Operating in a high rise, high quality office estate Estate transactions NEBOSH qualification The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best ’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform your recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. If you have an accessibility requirement, disability, or condition that means you might require changes to the recruitment process, please contact your recruiter to discuss this further. Our aim is to make you application as easy as possible, and your recruiter will be happy to work with you to make any necessary arrangements where possible. Benefits Our competitive benefits scheme gives you the opportunity to create a personalised benefits package, tailored to suit your lifecycle. You can this this allowance to purchase additional benefits such as dental or cycle to work, or you have the option to top up your base salary by taking this as cash. Core benefits that you will receive as standard are: 30 days holiday per year plus bank holidays Private healthcare with Bupa A non-contributory Pension of at least 8% of basic salary each month (there are several contribution levels that increase depending on your age- up to 12% a month once you reach age 35) Life assurance of eight times your basic salary Income protection Conflicts of interest All applicants to the FCA are required to demonstrate that they do not have other interests likely to conflict with their responsibilities as an employee of the FCA. You should declare any potential conflict of interest as early as possible in the selection process, and also disclose information or personal connections that, if appointed, might be open to misperception. Any potential conflicts of interest will not prevent candidates going forward to interview but may, if appropriate , be explored during the interview to establish how the candidate would address the issue(s) should they be successful in their application. Useful information The closing date for this role is 23:55 on Sunday 20 September Selection will be via a two-stage interview and psychometric assessment If successful, you will be required to obtain and retain SC Clearance. From September 2026, FCA employees will be required to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office. Our Executive Director and Directors will be expected to be in a minimum of 60% per month. The salary range for the role is £1 30 , 0 00- £150,000 This role will be London based only To apply please submit your CV and cover letter , using this link www.odgers.com/96619 The FCA has retained Odgers to look after this role on our behalf. The following link will take you to the Odgers website where you will be able to apply www.odgers.com/96619 If you have any questions regarding your application, please contact Peter Lawrence on Peter.Lawrence@odgers.com

item.title: Senior Associate – Market Research Manager
item.description: Job Title: Senior Associate – Market Research M anager Division : Supervision , Policy and Competition Directorate: Cross Cutting Policy & Strategy Department : Cross-Cutting Response, Research & Contracts Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,199 and London £59,200 to £73,799 per annum (Salary offered will b e based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your recruitment contact is: Louis Van den Burg via Louis.vandenburg@fca.org.uk Your External Recruitment contact is : Tahir Kahn via Tahir.Khan1@fca.org.uk Application must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. You will need a CV and a supporting statement no longer than 500 words . T he supporting statement is mandatory . Applications without a covering letter may not be accepted . We are also advertising for a Research Specialist ( JR0022287 ). You can apply for both roles through one application . Please indicate in your supporting statement if you are interested in, and why you are suitable for, both roles . About the FCA and the team The FCA regulates the conduct of c 3 5 , 5 00 firms in the UK to ensure our financial markets are honest, fair and competitive. Follow this link to find out more About the FCA . The FCA’s Market Research team provides vital consumer insights that support regulatory decisions. They deliver the Financial Lives survey (FLS) – a key, nationally representative study tracking UK consumer s’ attitudes, behaviours and financial experiences. The team also conducts bespoke surveys and qualitative research for other areas of the FCA, collaborates with third-party data providers and ensures consumer insights are embedded across the organisation. Their work informs policy, identifies emerging issues and measures regulatory impact – helping to keep the consumer voice central to financial oversight. The team also ma nages a smaller amount of firm research, inc ludin g res earch about the perce ptions firm s an d ot her sta kehol der s have of the FCA and how fir ms exper ience r egu latio n . Role r esponsibilities The role will be around 50 % on FLS, and around 5 0 % on bespoke research , focused on research management . You will work closely with the team leads (Lead Associates) for FLS and for Bespoke research. You will e nsur e FLS is delivered to time and budget through excellent timetabling , coordinating dependencies across workstreams and suppliers , resource allocation, progress monitoring , supplier manage ment and stakeholder engagement . This will include w orking wi th the t eam t o man age respon ses to the many queries we receive for FLS analysis in FCA papers and publications . It will al so inclu de mana ging the MI ( ma nagemen t informa tion ) we col lect on the types of queries we rec e ive and from w hich p art s of the b usiness . Yo u will also manag e the internal governance processes to sign off FLS publications . Contracts are in place with 4 agencies for FLS up till wave 7 ending in 2031. You will manage the FLS budget spreadsheet, liaise with suppliers monthly to agree invoice amounts and produce a monthly summary for Finance. You will also produce forecasts as required by Finance . FLS runs on a 2 year cycle, meaning that every 2 years you will manage the process of reagreeing scope and costs with suppliers for the upcoming wave. Within each 2-year wave, you will manage contract variations, as needed . You will also provide project management support for the procurement and delivery of bespoke market research projects , through excellent timetabling, resource allocation, progress monitoring, supplier management and stakeholder engagement . An important task will be to help build and maintain the pipeline of work coming into the team . We have a Market Research Framework in place, to source suppliers – th is will be renewed in 2028, and you will have a sub stant ial role in planning this renewal from around mid 2027 . There is an option for you to run smaller bespoke projects, ie working on the research it self ( eg design , analysis and r eporting) , s ubject to your availability and interests . You will also support stakeholder engagement and communications planning to maximise the value of all the Market Research Team’s outputs , helping to ensur e they are embedded in publications, speeches, policy development, supervision work and strategic decision-making. Finally, you will c ontribute to w ider team management , including recruitment coordination, man a ging the agendas for team meetings and heredays , updating FCA systems about the data we hold and any risks we own, and continuous improvement of Market Research Team processes and record-keeping . Skills Required Minimum Prior experience managing market research projects within a market research agency , regulator or government department , including devising and overseeing workstreams and detailed timelines as well as overseeing suppliers . Strong organisational skills, with the ability to work autonomously and del iver on your ow n ini tiati ve , to manage competing priorities, to work collaboratively to ac hieve wider tea m goals , and to keep delivery on track. High attention to detail, with the ability to implement and maintain processes that ensure the quality and rigour of the team’s work . Essential Good knowledge of a broad range of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies , with e xperience in survey design, questionnaire development, and analysis and reporting. With these skills, you will be able to help the team create and keep to workable projects and project timelines . Ability to manage complex timelines and capacity plans ( eg using Gantt charts and Excel) , adapting delivery to changing priorities, resource constraints and competing demands . Excellent team-working skills to support the team and help them to manage their own resource and priorities . Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to engage senior colleagues, subject matter experts, operational teams and suppliers . Experience of managing research budgets , with a high level of ability in Excel for this . Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where employees currently work a minimum of 5 0% in the office each month A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes , we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.description: Job Title: Senior Associate – Market R esearch specialist Division : Supervision , Policy and Competition Directorate: Cross Cutting Policy & Strategy Department : Cross-Cutting Response, Research & Contracts Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,199 and London £59,200 to £73,799 per annum (Salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your recruitment contact is: Louis Van den Burg via Louis.vandenburg@fca.org.uk Your External Recruitment contact is : Tahir Kahn via Tahir.Khan1@fca.org.uk Application must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. You will need a CV and a supporting statement no longer than 500 words . T he supporting statement is mandatory . P l ease i nclude links to an y research publ icatio ns. Applications without a covering letter may not be accepted . We are also advertising for a Research Manager ( JR0022259 ). You can apply for both roles through one application . Please indicate in your supporting statement if you are interested in, and why you are suitable for, both roles . About the FCA and the team The FCA regulates the conduct of c 3 5 , 5 00 firms in the UK to ensure our financial markets are honest, fair and competitive. Follow this link to find out more About the FCA . The FCA’s Market Research team provides vital consumer insights that support regulatory decisions. The team conducts bespoke surveys and qualitative research for other areas of the FCA, collaborates with third-party data providers and ensures consumer insights are embedded across the organisation. They also deliver the Financial Lives survey (FLS) – a key, nationally representative study tracking UK consumer s’ attitudes, behaviours and financial experiences. Their work informs policy, identifies emerging issues and measures regulatory impact – helping to keep the consumer voice central to financial oversight. The tea m also ma nages a smaller amount of firm research, inc ludin g res earch about the perce ptions firm s an d ot her sta kehol der s have of the FCA and how fir ms exper ience r egu latio n . Role r esponsibilities The role will be around 75% on bespoke research and around 25% on FLS . You will work closely with the team leads (Lead Associates) for FLS and for Bespoke research. You will work with our internal clients, to write excellent Statements of Requirements ( SoRs ) for new bespoke research , assess/ evaluate agency bids, and work with appointed suppliers to ensure research projects are delivered on time and within budget. You will be responsible for ensuring that projects use optimal data collection , data is robust, and findings are analysed and reported well. For quantitative bespoke projects you will ensure that sampling, screening and weigh t ing are addressed as early as needed in the project timeline, and that outputs will meet client needs . For qual itative research you will ensure pro jects meet client needs , wh ether they are standalone projects , or intended to help design a survey or to fill the gaps quantitative research cannot fill, or to inform be havioural testing research run by our colleagues in Economics. For some projects, you r role may be to design the survey or t he qualitat ive research , and/or to provide in a SoR a clear research design for agencies to refine. So met imes y ou wi ll produc e a first draft o f the questi onnai re or discuss ion guide . You will be responsible for two or three of the retail financial sectors or topics covered by the FLS, meaning you deliver the questionnaire, the tabspec and the slides-based report for these sections of the survey. item.title: Lead Delivery Engineer
item.description: Lead Delivery Engineer, Technology Directorate Location - Leeds Permanent Full Time Flexible Working Options: This role is open to flexible working patterns. These may include: Flexible start and end time to each day. Ability to adapt calendar as needed, for example to fit in the school run, gym or appointments. A 50% in-office attendance requirement that can be spread across the month to accommodate diverse working patterns, such as the flexibility to purchase a weekly train ticket for certain weeks. Working from abroad policy, subject to approval and policy within the team. The Technology Directorate provides information and system technology services to all business areas in the Bank as part of Central Services. Our key objective is to support the policy and operational divisions to meet the Bank’s stated objectives. An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Azure and M365 Specialist to join the Digital Workplace team. This role will work as part of the wider Microsoft 365 team within Digital Workplace, a function responsible for delivering and supporting the collaboration, productivity and information management services used across the Bank. The team owns and supports core Microsoft 365 services including SharePoint, Teams, Copilot, and related information governance capabilities, alongside specialist information management and preservation platforms. We want to make more of the technology that we have and explore opportunities to use it in new ways to make the Bank more effective. The successful candidate will bring Azure cloud experience to help design, implement and support automation solutions, service integrations and technical improvements across Microsoft 365 technologies and services. The role combines technical problem solving, stakeholder engagement, cloud engineering and continual service improvement, while contributing to the wider evolution of Digital Workplace services. This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys learning new technologies, working closely with business stakeholders, and improving services that deliver long-term organisational value. A typical day could start with a sprint stand-up with the wider team, checking progress against current priorities and agreeing how to unblock delivery. You might then join project meetings with stakeholders, take part in solution design conversations with technical colleagues, or raise change requests for product or service changes. At lunch time, you could head over to the office canteen to have a break with your colleagues, then head to an event organised by an employee network. For the second half of the day, you might be investigating incidents impacting the team’s Azure-hosted solutions, troubleshooting service issues and identifying improvements to prevent recurrence. Finally, you might dedicate some time to review upcoming changes from Microsoft to identify risks and opportunities. Key Responsibilities • Design and implement best practice Azure-based solutions that integrate with core Microsoft 365 products to improve business processes and information management outcomes. • Support Azure-hosted services and manage associated cloud resources used by the wider Digital Workplace team. • Investigate, troubleshoot and resolve technical incidents, problems and service requests at a third line level. • Document technical solutions, support procedures and operational processes. • Share knowledge with colleagues and contribute to the development of technical capability within the wider team. • Identify opportunities to improve service reliability, supportability, automation and user experience. Minimum Criteria • Experience supporting, administering or implementing Microsoft Azure cloud solutions in an enterprise environment, including services that integrate with Microsoft 365 technologies. • Experience administering core Microsoft 365 services such as SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business and Teams. • Ability to gather requirements, assess service improvement opportunities and independently design practical technical solutions that improve supportability, automation or user experience. • Strong troubleshooting, documentation and communication skills, with experience supporting business-critical services and working effectively across technical and business teams. Essential Criteria • A proactive approach to service improvement and knowledge sharing. • Awareness of how information governance, records management, compliance and data lifecycle principles influence the design and operation of workplace technology services. • Ability to build effective working relationships with stakeholders, suppliers and technical teams, translating needs into practical, well-governed outcomes. • Strong analytical judgement, with the ability to understand complex issues, evaluate options and recommend proportionate solutions. • Technical curiosity and learning agility, with enthusiasm for exploring new technologies, building knowledge independently and acting as a trailblazer for emerging capabilities. • A continuous improvement mindset, with the confidence to challenge existing ways of working and help shape better, more sustainable service outcomes. Desirable Criteria • Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio or AI Foundry, including exploring practical use cases for AI-enabled productivity, automation or service improvement. • Power Platform technologies, particularly Power Automate and Power Apps, to deliver low-code automation and business process improvements. • APIs, automation technologies, systems integration or Infrastructure as Code and DevOps tooling. • Microsoft Purview, information governance, records management, document management, archival or digital preservation systems. • Working in a regulated, public sector or highly governed environment, including effective engagement with third-party suppliers. • Plus, any relevant Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Copilot or Power Platform certifications. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Leeds Salary: £49,360 - £55,530 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application ques

item.title: Enforcement Investigator
item.description: Job Title: Enforcement Investigator Division: Enforcement & Market Oversight Department : Retail and Regulatory Investigations Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £47,200 to £62,900 and London from £50,300 to £67,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Associate – Level 8 - Practising Legal For Internal candidates, your recruitment contact is Rhianna via rhianna.walkden@fca.org.uk For External candidates, your recruitment contact is Riley via riley.fox@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. Enforcement & Market Oversight (EMO) is responsible for the FCA’s responsibilities for market monitoring, delivery of the functions of the UK Listing Authority (UKLA) and the investigation and prosecution of misconduct using the whole spectrum of criminal, civil and administrative sanctions and remedies against firms and individuals. Retail and Regulatory Investigations (RRI) investigates potential misconduct by regulated firms and individuals working within those firms, involved in retail banking, stockbroking, asset management, mortgage broking and lending, insurance intermediation, financial advice, consumer credit and payment services. We take action against firms that sell unsuitable products or services to consumers, mishandle client money and assets, or have governance and systemic issues. We also investigate financial crime matters including fraud and misconduct related to AML systems and controls. Role responsibilities Associates are involved at every stage of the investigation process, supporting your team, developing your knowledge and sharing your experience, which includes: Taking on differing degrees of responsibility for a mixture of cases depending on their nature and complexity. This could range from playing a leading role in smaller cases with management oversight, to working as part of a wider team on larger more complex cases Progressing a portfolio of investigations, managing your work to meet competing deadlines. Obtaining evidence through the use of appropriate tools and powers and developing the case team’s understanding. Exploring detailed evidence and making recommendations Drafting all forms of case documents (which may include witness statements, civil orders, statutory notices and papers going before the Regulatory Decision Committee) and correspondence with investigation subjects, their legal representatives and witnesses Participating in challenging interviews of subjects and witnesses using compulsory powers, on a voluntary basis and under caution Preparing for and presenting cases at, internal case committees when required Where appropriate, provide legal advice to the case team and where appropriate take responsibility for the preparation of privileged correspondence Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of analysing large amounts of information and producing summaries which make conclusions and draw out key findings You must hold a valid practising certificate issued by the Solicitors Regulation Authority for England and Wales (if a solicitor), or the General Council of the Bar for England and Wales (if a barrister) (or a similar internationally recognised qualification) Essential: Demonstrated experience supporting and progressing investigations or complex projects involving large volumes of information Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including in challenging or sensitive contexts Experience working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and managing competing priorities across multiple workstreams Clear written and verbal communication skills, including producing clear, structured written outputs and presenting findings or recommendations Relevant experience in financial services and/or fraud investigation/litigation Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values & culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. item.title: Technical Product Manager (DevOps)
item.description: Technical Product Manager (DevOps), Technology Directorate Location: Leeds or London Permanent Full Time Job Description RTGS is the Bank of England's Real Time Gross Settlement service, critical national infrastructure that underpins the UK financial system, settling hundreds of billions of pounds each day. We are looking for a Technical Product Manager to help shape and evolve the platform services that enable software delivery across RTGS Technology. Working within the Runtime Platform & Developer Experience domain, you will own the roadmap, epics, backlog and demand management processes for the engineering platforms and services that enable software delivery across RTGS Technology. You will work closely with engineers, architects, Software Engineering Team Leads and stakeholders to understand platform needs, shape demand and ensure platform capabilities evolve in line with technology strategy, engineering priorities, lifecycle obligations and operational requirements. This role sits at the intersection of platform engineering, software delivery and product management. You will own a balanced roadmap that ensures platform services remain secure, resilient, supportable and fit for the future. Working with engineers and stakeholders, you will prioritise demand, reduce operational toil through automation, manage technology lifecycle obligations and improve the effectiveness of software delivery across RTGS Technology. Acting as a steward of engineering capacity, you will help maintain a sustainable delivery model that balances operational responsibilities, platform evolution and continuous improvement. This is an opportunity to shape the future of engineering platforms within RTGS Technology and help enable the delivery of one of the UK's most critical technology services. Flexible Working Options This role is open to flexible working patterns, these may include: Flexible start and end time to each day Ability to adapt calendar as needed, this could be to fit in the school run, gym, or appointments A 50% in-office attendance requirement can be spread across the month to accommodate diverse working patterns, such as the flexibility to purchase a weekly train ticket for certain weeks Working from abroad policy (subject to approval and policy within the team) A Day in the Role One day you could be working with engineering teams to understand challenges within the software delivery lifecycle and identify opportunities to improve platform capabilities and engineering effectiveness. You may be working with Software Engineering Team Leads, architects and stakeholders to review roadmap priorities, balance competing demands and make informed trade-offs across platform improvements, lifecycle management, resilience, automation and operational support. At the same time, you could be working with platform engineers to prioritise upgrades, patching activities, technology refresh, obsolescence remediation and operational improvements, ensuring the team maintains the right balance between supporting today's services and investing in tomorrow's platform. No two days will be the same, but the focus remains consistent: maintaining a sustainable roadmap, evolving platform capabilities and enabling engineering teams to deliver software safely, efficiently and at scale. Role Requirements You will be responsible for translating engineering needs, operational requirements and technology priorities into a coherent and sustainable roadmap for Runtime Platform & Developer Experience services. Own the creation, maintenance and ongoing evolution of the roadmap, epics and backlog for Runtime Platform & Developer Experience services. Work closely with engineering teams and platform consumers to understand needs, identify opportunities for improvement and shape platform priorities through workshops, discovery activities and collaborative planning. Ensure engineering capacity is allocated appropriately across platform evolution, lifecycle management, operational support, resilience, automation and continuous improvement activities. Use feedback, operational insights and service data to identify bottlenecks, inform prioritisation decisions and drive continuous improvement. Maintain a balanced roadmap that supports platform reliability, lifecycle management, resilience, automation, developer experience and continuous improvement. Drive lifecycle management activities including patching, upgrades and obsolescence remediation whilst identifying opportunities to reduce operational effort through automation and standardisation. Work closely with Software Engineering Team Leads, architects and platform engineers to shape future platform direction. Challenge demand that could lead to unsustainable delivery or compromise long-term platform health. Communicate priorities, risks, dependencies and outcomes to stakeholders. Minimum Criteria We’re looking for someone who has the following key skills and experience: Experience managing roadmaps, backlogs, epics or prioritisation processes within a technology organisation. Experience working with engineering, technology or platform teams. Experience facilitating workshops, discovery activities or stakeholder engagement sessions. Experience improving operational processes, engineering effectiveness or service outcomes. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills. Understanding of Agile delivery and product management practices. Essential Criteria We are interested in hearing from candidates who have the following capabilities: Proven experience as a Product Manager, Technical Product Manager, Platform Product Manager or similar role within a technology environment. Experience owning roadmaps, epics and backlogs for technical products, platforms or services. Experience working within a software -or platform engineering environment. Strong understanding of software delivery, CI/CD, developer tooling, platform engineering concepts and modern engineering practices. Experience working closely with engineering teams, architects and technical stakeholders. Experience facilitating workshops and collaborative discovery activities. Experience defining and prioritising platform capabilities based on user needs, operational requirements and strategic objectives. Experience using feedback, operational insights and adoption data to shape roadmap decisions. Experience balancing platform evolution, lifecycle obligations, resilience, operational requirements and engineering productivity. Experience managing or prioritising work relating to platform lifecycle management, technology obsolescence, patching, upgrades or operational resilience. Strong planning, facilitation and stakeholder management skills. Ability to understand technical concepts and translate them into prioritised outcomes. Strong communication skills and ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders. Desirable Criteria It would also be beneficial, but not necessary, to have some of the following: Experience improving software delivery processes or engineering productivity. Experience using techniques such as value stream mapping, process mapping, journey mapping or similar approaches to identify improvement opportunities. Experience driving automation and operational efficiency initiatives. Experience with cloud and on-premise platform environments. Experience in financial services, payments or regulated environments. Knowledge of operational resilience, observability and technology lifecycle management practices. Don't hesitate to apply if you don't meet all the essential criteria. We value diverse perspectives and believe that different backgrounds can contribute to our team's success. How This Role Fits into the Wider Bank RTGS Technology is undergoing a significant transformation, moving to a product engineering model with teams aligned to business and platform domains. The Technical Product Manager reports to the Technology Product Lead and forms part of the Product Management function within RTGS Technology. This role exists to ensure RTGS engineering teams have secure, reliable and sustainable platform services that enable them to develop, deploy and operate software efficiently whilst maintaining long-term platform health and operational resilience. The Technical Product Manager owns the roadmap, epics and backlog for Runtime Platform & Developer Experience services, ensuring demand is prioritised and engineering capacity is directed towards the highest-value outcomes. Success in this role will be measured through improvements in engineering effectiveness, operational resilience, successful lifecycle management, reduction in manual effort through automation and the maintenance of a sustainable delivery model that enables continuous improvement without compromising operational stability. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. (Salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Lead Associate, Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal.
