By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Cyber and Information Resilience (C&IR) is responsible for the management of cyber security at the FCA. 'Cyber security' means the protection of the FCA's data and systems from malicious activity, including theft, damage and disruption, in order that the FCA can deliver its key business functions. C&IR is now part of a new formed Directorate lead by our CISO, Director of Cyber & Operational Resilience Division. ​​​​​​The role is based in the Cyber Assurance team, who leads on the FCA & PSR cyber assurance activities working to determine that correct cyber assurance and control measures are in place. The team conducts thorough reviews, analysis and testing to confirm the appropriate security and data controls (whether through technology, process, or behaviour) and the secure operation of the FCA systems and data are in place Role responsibilities Lead the FCA's Data Security Assurance Framework, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, availability and appropriate use of corporate data, aligned to the FCA's Cyber Risk Management Framework, regulatory, legislative and internal control requirements Establish and deliver risk-based data security assurance across the FCA's data estate, including M365 security and compliance, cloud platforms, data lakes, AI systems and data repositories, ensuring the identification, assessment and treatment of security and data risks in line with the FCA's Cyber Risk Management Framework and associated tooling Drive the strategic evolution of the FCAs data security posture management for AI, assessing and assuring technical controls, data exposure and appropriate use across emerging AI capabilities such as MS Co-pilot, Agentic AI and AI-enabled platforms, ensuring security by design, effective data security governance and continuous assurance as the FCAs AI estate evolves Produce meaningful KPIs, KRIs, risk assessments and management information to support senior management decision-making, alignment with the FCA's Cyber Risk Management Framework and effective second-line Risk and Compliance oversight, while leading issue identification, remediation tracking and validation of corrective actions Lead and develop the FCA's Data Security Assurance capability, working across technology, cyber security, risk, compliance and data governance teams to embed effective controls throughout the data lifecycle, integrate assurance into the wider cyber risk management ecosystem and support consistent risk reporting, governance and oversight. Skills required Minimum: Proven experience leading a data security, cyber security, information security or assurance capability within a complex organisation, including building, developing and maturing teams, operating models and security capabilities Demonstrable experience designing, implementing and assuring data security controls and frameworks across SaaS, cloud and enterprise environments, aligned to recognised frameworks such as NIST CSF and ISO 27001 Strong understanding of data security principles and risks, including data discovery, data lineage, encryption, logging, access control, identity management, data loss prevention and protection against data exposure and exfiltration Essential: Experience delivering security assurance and risk assessments across applications, cloud platforms, data repositories, AI systems and broader technology environments, supported by continuous monitoring, control health reviews and risk reporting Experience establishing governance, assurance and control oversight processes, including attestations, control validation, remediation tracking and risk-based prioritisation Strong expertise in Microsoft Purview and Microsoft 365 security and compliance capabilities, including data discovery, classification, sensitivity labelling, DLP, Insider Risk Management, DSPM for AI and related E5 functionality Knowledge of regulatory, legal and compliance requirements relevant to data security and experience translating these into practical controls, assurance activities and risk management outcomes Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across technology, cyber security, data governance and business teams and to communicate complex security risks and control issues to senior leadership and executive stakeholders Experience integrating security tooling, telemetry, APIs and automation to improve assurance, risk visibility and control effectiveness across Microsoft, AWS and interconnected technology platforms Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with experience developing data security roadmaps, identifying emerging risks and driving improvements that strengthen organisational security posture Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in item.title: Security Control Room Officer in Security Operations - Debden Site
item.description: Location : Debden, Essex Department Overview The Security Operations team sits within the Bank of England’s Security Division and plays a vital role in protecting our people, tenants, visitors, buildings, assets and information. As part of the UK’s Critical National Infrastructure, and with responsibility for supporting the production of all Bank of England banknotes, our security environment is high-profile, complex and closely connected with law enforcement. This is an interesting and varied opportunity to join an organised, disciplined and professional team at the heart of the UK’s central bank. The Security Operations team is structured to provide flexibility, enabling colleagues to train, test and exercise while continuing to deliver essential day-to-day security operations. The team works closely with stakeholders across all business areas, making this a broad and engaging role in a unique security environment. Job Description As a Control Room Operator, you will work under the direction of the Security Control Room Shift Leader to help protect the Bank from internal and external physical security threats and support responses to infrastructure failures in partnership with others. This is a 24/7 operational role, working on a rotational shift pattern. The role focuses on overseeing IDS and CCTV systems, managing key communication activity and applying Bank-specific knowledge to support security requirements across different business areas. You will make security decisions in line with standard operating procedures, with support from senior colleagues where needed, and may occasionally direct contractor staff. Role Responsibilites As a Security Control Room Operator, you will play a key role in helping to protect the Bank of England’s people, buildings, assets and information. Working as part of a 24/7 security operation, your main responsibility will be to monitor and respond to physical security risks, internal incidents and infrastructure failures, using established procedures and the support of senior colleagues where needed. You will oversee key security systems including CCTV, alarms and other monitoring equipment, assess and escalate potential threats, and coordinate effective responses to a range of situations. These may include suspicious activity, protests, bomb warnings, crime, fire, flood, first aid incidents, security breaches and other emergencies. A typical shift may involve; control room duties, static guarding, patrolling, searching, visitor management, emergency response, mail examination, building protection, alarm monitoring, CCTV surveillance and asset protection. You will also take part in regular training, development and exercising activity to help maintain a high standard of operational readiness. This is a varied and responsible role that requires sound judgement, clear communication, strong attention to detail and the ability to remain calm under pressure. You will work closely with security colleagues, teams across the Bank, contractors and, when required, external emergency services to support a safe and secure environment. You will be required to work shifts which is predominantly a 3 on / 3 off rotation, but with two additional training days per month. This is a combination of early, late and night shifts on a rotation system. Hours of working are approximately 9 hours per shift and for training days. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Proven experience working in the security industry, a control room environment, or a high-security site. Demonstrable experience using security systems such as CCTV, alarm systems and/or fire systems. Able to work a 24/7 rotational shift pattern, including early, late and night shifts. Able to communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, including recording incidents and actions accurately. Essential Criteria Demonstrates sound judgement, integrity and professionalism when handling security-related matters. Able to remain calm, focused and effective when responding to incidents, alarms, emergency situations or competing priorities. Demonstrates good customer focus and the ability to provide a professional service to staff, visitors, contractors and stakeholders. Able to plan, prioritise and coordinate resources or activities effectively in response to operational requirements. Able to follow standard operating procedures and escalate security incidents appropriately when required. Demonstrates flexibility and reliability in supporting a shift-based operational environment. Desirable Criteria Holds a valid SIA Licence, security qualification or equivalent relevant qualification. Experience delivering a professional customer experience in a security, front-of-house, control room or operational environment. Experience supporting incident response, emergency procedures, access control, searching, patrolling or visitor management a Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information This role offers a salary of £28,640 and an annual, non-pensionable shift allowance of £8,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. item.title: Maintenance Technician in Property, Central Operations - London Sites
item.description: Location: London Sites Overview The Bank of England is the UK’s central bank, with a mission to promote the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability. Our Property department plays a key role in supporting that mission by keeping the Bank’s buildings safe, operational and effective for colleagues across a complex, high-profile estate. About the role As an Engineering Shift Technician in Infrastructure Engineering, you’ll help maintain the critical building systems that support the Bank’s 24/7 operations. This hands-on role covers planned, preventative and reactive maintenance across critical, essential and non-essential systems, where reliability, safety, service and professionalism are central to everything we do. Key responsibilities Deliver planned, preventative and reactive maintenance through Planon IWMS, including accurate and timely updates via handheld HMI devices. Carry out daily and periodic checks, routine maintenance and statutory testing across HVAC, BMS, electrical, public health, fire, life safety, critical assets and other building engineering systems. Respond to engineering faults and failures in line with priority response and fix times, helping maintain safe environments and minimise disruption to the Bank’s operations. Support specialist OEM contractors with planned maintenance, reactive tasks and emergency call-outs. Provide accurate data for daily shift handover logs, reports, incident management and recovery exercises. Act as, or support, an Authorised Person for LV electrical and/or mechanical systems, working within Safe Systems of Work to support 24/7 operations. Champion health and safety, ensuring work is delivered in line with agreed methods, risk assessments, service levels and customer service standards. Contribute to the Bank’s collaborative, continuous improvement culture by sharing ideas, innovation and practical improvements. Participate in the weekly on-call technical support rota to support incident response, if required. About you Role Requirements Minimum criteria City & Guilds Level 3, or equivalent transferable qualification, in a relevant engineering discipline. IOSH Operating Safely qualification. Experience using IWMS planned and reactive maintenance tools, including handheld HMI devices. Experience operating and maintaining HVAC, BMS, electrical, public health and life safety systems. Demonstrable Authorised Person experience in HV or LV system operation, with experience working within defined Safe Systems of Work. Knowledge of statutory and compliance obligations relevant to engineering systems. Ability to follow Standard Operating Procedures and Emergency Operating Procedures, and read complex mechanical, electrical, control and public health drawings. Essential criteria Proven understanding of building services and maintenance risk management. Experience producing clear reports and tailored communications. Track record of applying procedures to support decisions and improvements. Practical experience collaborating to deliver agreed outcomes. Successful delivery of quality work, customer service and maintenance outcomes. Experience prioritising workloads and remaining resilient under pressure. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information The salary for this role is £32,220. In addition, we also offer 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits We also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. item.title: Cyber Analyst in CYBER DEFENCE CENTRE
item.description: Cyber Analyst, Technology Directorate Permanent Full Time Leeds or London The Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) is responsible for detecting and responding to cyber-attacks against the Bank of England. Whilst the team is primarily located in the Bank's London office in Threadneedle Street, the team does also have a presence in the Leeds office. This posting is therefore open to London OR Leeds applicants. Department overview: Within the Cyber Security Division you will be working with people who are passionate about protecting the security and stability of our Technology estate. Whether it is identifying threats, uncovering vulnerabilities or ensuring robust and resilient infrastructure, you’ll be working at the cutting edge in a security-centric organisation. You’ll focus on ensuring security by design, and ensuring we have safe, stable and resilient systems. Collaborating closely with colleagues across Technology and throughout the organisation you will help the division safeguard critical systems and information. Our award-winning specialist teams are committed to developing their expertise in a constantly evolving environment. Aligned to industry best-practice, staff are encouraged to develop their skills both internally and externally, through mentoring, training and formal qualifications. Job description The Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) is responsible for detecting and responding to cyber-attacks against the Bank of England. The CDC is made up of four key domains: Capability, Threat, Detection Engineering and Defence Operations. Reporting to the Cyber Defence Operations Lead Operations lead in the Cyber Defence Operations (CDO) function, The successful candidate will take part in the operations rota ensuring security alerts are thoroughly investigated, escalated appropriately and take part in subsequent Cyber Security incident response activities as part of the wider Cyber Security incident response team where required. When not responding to security alerts or incidents, as part of the CDO function, the role holder will be expected to proactively seek opportunities to improve the team’s operational capability for both detection and response processes through a greater use of automation. The role will require close collaboration across all of the CDC’s core functions and has varied and challenging day-to-day responsibilities, as well as exposure to a range of cutting-edge technology in cyber security, data analytics and cyber threat intelligence. Key Experience / Skills Minimum: Good understanding of best practice security incident response concepts and approaches Practical experience in technical cyber security incident response methodologies Excellent written and verbal communication skills Essential: Experience working in Security Operations Centre with specific experience triaging security alerts and an understanding of wider cyber security incident response practices. Knowledge of computer network fundamentals, including network protocols and infrastructure (packet capture analysis, firewalls, web proxies, DNS etc.) Ability to convey complex information in a clear and concise manner Ability and willingness to learn new technical cyber security skills Logical mind-set Desirable: Experience developing and documenting incident response processes and designing IR playbooks. GCIH or similar qualification in Security Incident response The ability to acquire DV clearance (To be eligible to apply you must be a British citizen (either born here or naturalised) and one of your parents must be a British citizen or have substantial ties to the UK. Understanding of common cyber threats and attacker tactics, techniques and procedures and an ability to identify appropriate mitigation strategies Experience using automation or SOAR platforms Knowledge of incident response principles Experience using MITRE ATT&CK Experience using Splunk Experience using an intelligence platform Software development, scripting or programming skills Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. item.title: Senior Manager, Business Manager, Office of CIO in TECHNOLOGY
item.description: Senior Manager, Business Manager, Office of CIO in Technology Directorate Permanent Full Time Leeds or London Part of the Bank’s Technology Leadership Team and reporting to the Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Central Services COO, this role provides the business management, governance and operational oversight needed to run safe, secure and resilient technology services for the Bank of England. As a member of the Technology Leadership Team, you will be individually and collectively responsible for the Bank’s information technology and computer systems, through which the Bank delivers its mission. You will lead the core OCIO disciplines that enable effective technology leadership, including financial management and reporting, strategic supplier management, resource and demand management, regulatory compliance, audit coordination, risk management and performance reporting. Core to your role will be building strong relationships with the CIO, the TLT and key partners across the Bank who work closely with the Technology Directorate, including Finance, Change and Planning, People, Risk, Procurement and other central functions. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. Primary accountabilities Management of finances, performance and financial reporting • You are responsible for maintaining oversight of the financial performance of the Technology Directorate. • You work with the finance business partner and CIO to support financial and business planning, including the setting of budgets. • You define and monitor key financial, operational and supplier performance metrics, using data and insight to support prioritisation, investment decisions and transparent reporting to senior governance forums. • You are responsible for the provision of accurate and timely financial information to the CIO and to Court. Strategic supplier management • You maintain oversight of the Technology Directorate’s strategic supplier management approach, ensuring key supplier relationships are aligned to technology priorities, service resilience, commercial value and the Bank’s risk appetite. • You oversee the use of supplier segmentation, account management plans, performance scorecards and relationship reviews to ensure strategic suppliers are managed according to their criticality, value and risk profile. • You monitor strategic supplier performance, contractual obligations, service levels, key risks, improvement actions and value delivery, ensuring issues are escalated through the appropriate governance forums. • You support executive engagement with strategic suppliers, helping the Technology Leadership Team move supplier relationships beyond tactical renewals towards long-term partnership, innovation, resilience and continuous improvement. • You ensure supplier insight, market intelligence and third-party risk information are used to inform technology planning, investment decisions, commercial pipelines and future sourcing strategies Internal process management • You maintain oversight of internal business processes that support Technology Directorate productivity, service quality, cost control and timely delivery. • You evaluate existing business processes, determining and outlining business process improvements. • You work with the Technology Leadership Team and other technology leaders to identify opportunities for innovation, automation, simplification and continuous improvement across Technology Directorate operations. • You work with the Change and Planning Directorate to oversee the implementation of Bank-wide business process improvement initiatives. Resource and demand management • You are responsible for maintaining oversight of overall headcount within the Technology Directorate to ensure the directorate operates within its headcount budget. • You support the capacity planning process as part of the budgeting and forecasting cycle, ensuring workforce plans are aligned to technology priorities, delivery commitments and affordability. • You work with the Change and Planning Directorate to ensure that change programmes are resourced appropriately. Regulatory compliance • You are responsible for ensuring the Technology Directorate complies with external regulatory requirements and internal policies, including public procurement policy, technology resilience obligations and compliance relating to Critical National Infrastructure. • You coordinate the gathering of internal information in response to regulatory requests. • You collaborate within the directorate and with partners across the Bank to foster a culture of compliance. Risk and audit management • You establish, maintain and review the Technology Directorate’s risk management framework, mechanisms and tools, ensuring they support consistent identification, assessment, monitoring, control and reporting of technology risk. • You support and monitor the first line of defence in applying technology risk management tools, including identifying, assessing, monitoring and controlling technology risk, and advising on proportionate mitigation measures. • You assess the adequacy and effectiveness of controls from a technology risk perspective during due diligence of new products and applications, incident handling and material change activity, providing advice and recommendations where required. • You collaborate within the directorate and with partners across the Bank to foster a shared understanding of risk. • You work with the TLT to support the management of Technology risks and controls. • You support the management of technology audit activity by coordinating evidence, tracking actions, monitoring closure of agreed mitigations and ensuring issues are escalated through the appropriate governance forums. • You coordinate the gathering of internal information in response to audit requests, ensuring responses are complete, timely and aligned with agreed ownership of audit actions. Team management and management of PS/PA office • You are accountable for building knowledge, skills and best practice within your teams and across the Technology Directorate. • You are responsible for developing and mentoring a high-performing team of direct reports. Role requirements Minimum/Essential criteria • Proven experience and track record of building relationships across business units and with a range of stakeholders, balancing competing interests and generating a collaborative, one-team mindset. • Successful leadership experience, established over several years, within a high-performing central operations or COO team, or in a comparable technology business management function. • Established understanding of finance, budgeting and forecasting, with an accounting qualification desirable, and experience using financial insight to support technology investment, supplier and workforce decisions. • Established understanding of regulatory compliance, audit management and risk management in a complex technology or regulated environment. • Established understanding of internal process management and capacity and demand planning. Strong stakeholder management and interpersonal skills • You have very strong interpersonal skills at senior levels and a proven ability to influence decisions across organisational boundaries. • You are an effective communicator, able to create a compelling narrative and inspire people to follow you. • You can build trusted relationships at all levels of the Bank, enabling you to have difficult conversations in pursuit of a common objective. You can make and recommend difficult decisions. • You are recognised as an empathetic people leader and a role model for the Bank’s leadership values, promoting an inclusive culture and working environment. An experienced ‘operator’ within a central operations team • You are an experienced technology business management operator, using financial, workforce, supplier and performance insight to influence the directorate’s budgeting and forecasting process and support delivery within agreed budgets. • You are an experienced capacity and demand planner, able to make and support recommendations about the directorate’s workforce while balancing stakeholder needs and understanding due process. • You have demonstrable understanding of regulatory compliance within a comparable organisation. • You have demonstrable understanding of risk management processes within a comparable organisation. An ambassador for the Bank • You are able to build and tap into a wide external network to learn, attract talent, and help drive the reputation of the Bank. You might represent the Bank at relevant external engagements. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, div

item.title: AI Analyst
item.description: Job Title: AI Analyst Division: Data, Technology and Innovation Department: AI Product Development Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £72,000 and London from £59,200 to £80,000 per annum (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Benjamin via benjamin.paulon@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Pat via Patrycja.Matachowska@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Data, Technology and Innovation (DTI) division enables the FCA to be a digital-first, data-led smart regulator by delivering a secure, agile, and cost-effective technology and data ecosystem that drives better decisions, transparency, and operational efficiency. Sitting within DTI, the AI Product Development department scopes and shapes AI solutions across the FCA and helps manage the organisation-wide pipeline of AI initiatives, ensuring work is prioritised, well-defined and aligned to strategic outcomes. Role responsibilities Identify and shape high value opportunities for applying AI across the organisation, enabling smarter and more effective regulatory outcomes to maximise impact Facilitate structured discovery workshops with stakeholders to surface pain points, map processes and pinpoint where AI can deliver meaningful improvements that increase efficiency Build credibility and influence at all levels of the organisation, including senior leaders and decision-makers, adapting communication style and messages to suit different audiences and securing buy-in for AI-driven change and innovation initiatives Translate business challenges into clear functional and non-functional requirements, working collaboratively with technical teams to design AI enabled solutions that meet real needs Manage and prioritise a pipeline of AI initiatives, partnering with data scientists and leadership to focus effort on the highest impact projects for maximum value Contribute to the organisation’s wider AI adoption strategy through insight, stakeholder engagement, and evidence-based recommendations to guide direction Advocate best practice in business analysis, promoting consistency, quality and knowledge sharing across the department to develop capability Gain experience delivering experimental and innovative projects that address real world challenges such as financial crime and consumer protection to create tangible outcomes Build a distinctive skill set at the intersection of AI, data, technology and regulation within a collaborative, learning focused environment to support career growth Skills required Minimum: Experience in a senior business analyst role or a comparable position such as Consultant, Solution/Service Designer or Product Owner Experience delivering projects across the full lifecycle, using both waterfall and agile methodologies Working knowledge of artificial intelligence, including areas such as large language models (LLMs), agentic AI, and prompt engineering. Essential: Solid understanding of core Business Analysis techniques, including user journey mapping, process mapping, requirements gathering and the ability to design and facilitate collaborative workshops Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage, challenge and gain buy-in from senior leaders and subject matter experts across the organisation Ability to work through complex problems, identifying underlying issues and opportunities for improvement Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to adapt style, language and level of detail to different audiences, from technical specialists to senior executives, ensuring complex concepts are understood and acted upon Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to adapt style, language and level of detail to different audiences, from technical specialists to senior executives, ensuring complex concepts are understood and acted upon Experience navigating complex stakeholder environments, balancing competing priorities and influencing decisions with minimal supervision Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page. Our values & culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timeline Advert Closing: 6th September at 11:59pm CV Review/Shortlist: 14th September Interview W/C: 21st September Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time

item.title: Commercial Policy Manager (Sourcing)
item.description: Location: Leeds We have an exciting new role in the Commercial Policy and Operations team at the Bank, leading how we deliver commercial sourcing policy and providing expert support and guidance to the rest of the organisation. This role is part of the Commercial division’s Policy and Operations team, who deliver the policies, processes, systems and tools needed for the Bank to undertake commercial activity. The Team The team operates partly in a matrix management style, with most people dividing their time between their area of accountability (sourcing policy in this case) and pooled resource to work on cross-team projects. This enables the team to be dynamic and responsive around workload, drive collaboration and develop leadership skills at all levels. This role will be responsible for ensuring we have effective commercial sourcing policies, processes and guidance in place, as well as leading on cross-team projects in a matrix management setup. Role Responsibilities This role will be responsible for: Setting out the forward-looking strategy for sourcing policy in the Bank, defining what is needed in this area and developing a plan to deliver it. This should include the required stakeholder management, communications, etc. Creating and maintaining the Bank’s sourcing policies and processes. These should seamlessly integrate with any other areas of the commercial lifecycle, notably supplier management, third-party risk management and responsible procurement, and integrate considerations from key stakeholders such as Legal. The policies should align with public-sector legislation (including the National Procurement Policy Statement and applicable Procurement Policy Notes) and should be regularly reviewed and updated in line with benchmarking exercises, to ensure they reflect the latest best practice, and the processes should be continually improved to maximise efficiency and effectiveness. Ensuring colleagues involved in sourcing (both inside and outside of the Commercial division) understand their role and how the policies and processes should be applied, and are enabled to do this, by producing and sourcing appropriate and tailored templates, guidance and training, and ensuring they are communicated and delivered to them. Providing sourcing policy expert advice and support for more complex and specific queries not covered by the training and guidance, in line with the latest best practice. This will also include ensuring the sourcing policies are considered as part of commercial governance and offering technical advice on these considerations. Being able to evidence progress in the Bank’s approach to sourcing through the monitoring of key sourcing KPIs, such as compliance with notice publication requirements. Writing short business cases to support having access to the Policy team’s resource pool. You will also be part of a pool of resources across the team, enabling you to lead on some of the larger cross-team projects, depending on how workload varies across areas. These projects may cover matters across the whole of the Policy and Operations’ team scope. Although this is not a people management role, you will matrix manage other colleagues in the context of the projects you will lead. In those instances, you will be responsible for defining roles and responsibilities within your projects. You will develop the team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. You will also be expected to provide feedback to their line manager about their performance during your projects. Role Requirements Minimum criteria In-depth knowledge and experience of public-sector sourcing and current legislation Demonstrable experience of writing and rolling out public-sector sourcing policies Demonstrable knowledge of the rest of the commercial lifecycle (supplier management, responsible procurement and third-party risk management) Demonstrable knowledge of where and how to source the latest best-practice trends in public-sector sourcing Experience of creating and implementing strategies and delivery plans for their area of responsibility Ability to explain and present commercial matters to non-commercial colleagues, in the context of sourcing matters Essential criteria Excellent stakeholder management skills Excellent problem-solving skills Creative and critical thinking skills Self-motivation, with past evidence of driving own workload Excellent written and verbal communication skills Customer-focused, with experience delivering high-quality service and continuous improvement. Other criteria If you do not already have it, you would be expected to achieve Level 4 CIPS (funded by the Bank). Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information Location: Leeds This role offers an annual salary range in circa. of £46,320- £52,110 (depending on skills and experience). In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two stages. This role closes for applications on 15 September 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Senior Manager, Information Operations
item.description: The Bank of England (“the Bank”) is the UK's central bank. Our mission is to deliver monetary and financial stability for the British people. The Bank of England is a diverse organisation. Each of our 5000 people are committed to public service and dedicated to promoting the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability. Central Operations delivers critical functions that support the Bank’s effectiveness and resilience across security, procurement, sustainability and optimisation services. The Information Management division is a newly established function within Central Operations, providing integrated policy and governance, operational services and information platform leadership so information is secure, compliant, accessible and reusable. ROLE SUMMARY This role leads the Information Operations team within Information Management and serves as the Bank’s senior lead for operational information management services under the Head of Information Management. It is responsible for information access and disclosure services, records management operations, retention, review and deletion services, and the operational controls, processes and management information that support effective lifecycle delivery. The role leads the delivery and continuous improvement of core operational information management services, including Freedom of Information and Subject Access Request handling, records management operations, Red List administration, retention, review and deletion activity, and oversight of Tier 0 (self service) information controls. It provides leadership through team leaders across a multi-disciplinary operational team, ensuring services operate effectively, consistently and in line with statutory, regulatory and policy requirements, with clear operational controls, management information, escalation routes and management oversight. The role works closely with Information Policy, Information Platforms, Technology and business stakeholders to translate policy into operational processes, strengthen control effectiveness and support resilient, auditable service delivery across the information lifecycle. Key Responsibilities Operational Service Delivery and Control Lead the Bank’s operational information management services, ensuring delivery is effective, consistent and aligned with policy requirements, legal and regulatory obligations, service expectations and operational priorities. Oversee information access and disclosure services, including Freedom of Information, Subject Access Request and related operational processes, ensuring timely, accurate and well-governed delivery. Lead records management operations, including retention, review and deletion activity, ensuring processes are auditable, proportionate and consistently applied. Service Management, Risk and Continuous Improvement Establish and maintain effective service management arrangements, including prioritisation, service standards, controls, escalation routes, issue resolution and performance monitoring. Manage operational risks, issues and exceptions, ensuring material concerns are identified, escalated and addressed appropriately and that service delivery remains resilient and well controlled. Use operational data, management information and insight to improve performance, inform assurance activity and support continuous improvement across the wider Information Management function. Operational Delivery Model and Enterprise Alignment Work closely with Information Policy, Information Platforms, Technology, Legal, Privacy, Records Management and business stakeholders to embed policy and control requirements in operational processes and enterprise information platforms. Improve operational processes, workflows and service design to reduce manual effort, increase consistency and strengthen end-to-end lifecycle management across information services. Support the development of sustainable operating models for information services, ensuring roles, responsibilities and hand-offs are clear and effective across teams. Leadership and People Management Lead the Information Operations function through team leaders, setting direction and priorities across a multi-disciplinary operational team, ensuring effective management oversight, clear accountability and consistent delivery across services. Develop team leaders and build a strong culture of service, control, accountability and continuous improvement across the wider team. Minimum Criteria Experience leading operational information management, records management, disclosure, or relevant comparable services in a complex or regulated organisation. Experience establishing or running operational services with defined processes, controls, service standards, prioritisation and performance oversight. Experience managing statutory, regulatory or policy-led operational requirements, for example in records management, data protection, Freedom of Information, Subject Access Requests or similar controlled services. Experience leading teams through managers or team leaders, with accountability for delivery, control and service improvement. Essential Criteria Strong judgement and decision-making skills, with the ability to manage operational risk, resolve issues and escalate appropriately in a controlled environment. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain complex issues, trade-offs and priorities clearly to different audiences. Ability to lead through others, build capability in managers or team leaders and foster a culture of accountability, service and continuous improvement. Ability to work across organisational boundaries and translate policy, control or legal requirements into practical and proportionate operational delivery. Desirable Criteria Knowledge of records management, data protection, Freedom of Information and Subject Access Request requirements within a broader information management framework. Familiarity with enterprise information environments such as Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Purview or related technologies from an operational, records or disclosure perspective. Experience improving or redesigning operational processes to strengthen control, consistency or service efficiency. Experience working in a large, complex institutional environment and navigating multiple stakeholder groups, governance requirements and operational dependencies. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. ___ Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. For most roles where work can be carried out at home, we aim for colleagues to spend half of their time in the office, with a minimum of 40% per month. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them, their team and stakeholders. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Salary £81,600 - £91,800 per annum In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80 of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65 or 1/50) or decrease (to 1/95 or 1/105) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. item.title: Senior Associate – Freedom of Information Appeals
item.description: Senior Associate – Freedom of Information Appeals Division – Communications Department – Internal Communications, External Affairs & Public Information Team – Information Disclosure Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £43,300 to £60,000 and London from £46,400 to £64,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Corporate Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. In the Communications division at the FCA we change opinions and behaviours to enable a fair and thriving financial services market for the good of consumers and the economy. It’s an exciting time as we’re expanding our team and changing how we do things to deliver more engaging, insight-led, audience focused communications. If you want to be part of a supportive and fun team, work across a wide range of issues and are ready to be challenged, curious and creative then come and join us. The Information Disclosure and Appeals teams are responsible for managing Freedom of Information (FOI) requests, personal data access requests and related appeals. The team plays a key role in helping the FCA meet its statutory obligations, supporting our transparency agenda and ensuring compliance with information rights legislation. This role is critical in managing legal, regulatory and reputational risk, as failure to meet statutory deadlines could result in action from the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and impact confidence in the FCA as a regulator. Role responsibilities Manage FOIA appeals, including Internal Reviews, Information Commissioner investigations and First-tier Tribunal (Information Rights) appeals. Support the wider Information Disclosure team with the Publication Scheme, data protection witness statements and Re-use of Public Sector Information requests Produce high quality oral and written communications to key stakeholders and to members of the public (Requesters) Provide expert advice, training and guidance to stakeholders across the FCA, promoting awareness of FOIA requirements and ensuring the organisation remains informed of legislative and regulatory developments Oversee the triage and allocation of work, ensuring service levels and agreed SLAs are met Line manage and develop junior colleagues through coaching, mentoring and knowledge sharing, while acting as a key escalation point for complex and high-profile cases Skills required Minimum: Exceptional writing and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to explain complex disclosure-related issues to diverse audiences FOIA legislation experience and good knowledge of the ICO code of practice Experience researching regulatory developments and analysing information from multiple sources to identify risks, trends and emerging issues Essential: Excellent organisational skills with the ability to meet deadlines while maintaining high service standards Meticulous attention to detail in drafting responses, coupled with sound decision-making abilities Proven ability to build strong relationships and networks across an organisation to ensure a cohesive approach and timely delivery Ability to influence senior stakeholders through clear and persuasive guidance Proficiency in document redaction using various applications and software Demonstrated ability to lead, manage, coach, develop and motivate teams effectively Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert closes: Midnight, 13 September 2026 CV Review/Shortlist: 15 September 2026 Interview: 24 September and onwards 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time. SC Clearance is required for this role ( SC Guidance ) - you will hold or will be required to obtain Security Check (SC) level vetting

item.title: Senior Wholesale Brokers Supervisor
item.description: Job title: Senior Wholesale Brokers Supervisor Division: Supervision, Policy and Competition Department: Sell-Side Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £62,700 and London £59,200 to £69,000 per annum (Salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate, Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Shafika via Shafika.shaikh@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Iona.magee@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Sell-Side Directorate oversees wholesale banks, intermediaries, market infrastructure and exchanges, ensuring fair, transparent and resilient wholesale markets that support the effective functioning of the UK’s financial system. Role responsibilities Develop and deliver supervisory strategies across a portfolio of wholesale broker firms, aligning activities with regulatory priorities Develop and oversee supervisory workstreams from inception to completion, securing senior stakeholder agreement and driving successful execution Conduct thematic and multi-firm reviews to assess firms' governance, risk management frameworks, and operational resilience arrangements Directly supervise a portfolio of firms, taking ownership of complex supervisory cases, decisions, and regulatory interventions Assess and address issues relating to financial crime, market abuse, conduct risk, prudential resilience, and regulatory compliance Identify, investigate, and manage significant supervisory concerns, including serious misconduct allegations, business model risks, and potential firm failures. Build and maintain effective relationships with senior leaders at regulated firms to motivate, engage with, and support positive regulatory outcomes and also internal specialists across Policy, Market Monitoring, Prudential Supervision, Operational Risk, Financial Crime, Enforcement, and Legal teams Support the development of supervision strategies for colleagues' portfolios, contributing specialist knowledge and regulatory insight. Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of wholesale financial markets and regulation Prior experience exercising judgement in complex situations Prior experience in a role which has required strong written communication skills Essential: Knowledge of wholesale brokers, their business models and conduct risks arising from them, as well as of wholesale markets more generally The ability to assess complex information and form strong judgements Good awareness of the UK regulatory framework The ability to communicate with impact and influence at senior levels (in both verbal and written form) The ability to engage with a variety of internal and external stakeholders Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Advert Close Date: 16th September 2026 CV Review/Shortlist: 18th September 2026 First Interview: W/C 28th September 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time

item.title: Digital Project Manager
item.description: Digital Project Manager Full time / Part time Salary: £ 44,297 - £ 49,813 pa, with potential for further progression to £ 56,082 pa with our pay progression scheme. Location: Manchester Contracted to our Wilmslow office , we will be relocating to Manchester city centre from 28 September 2026. Once the move takes place your contracted office will be Circle Square, Manchester. Through hybrid working we offer flexible home and office-based working opportunities and there will be times when you will be expected to attend the office to collaborate with colleagues or travel due to business need. Why work for the ICO? Pay progression scheme . Hybrid and flexible working options. 25 days paid holiday per year, plus privilege and public holidays. Flexi leave (up to 26 additional days leave per year). Pension (employer contribution around 28.9 %). Online discount scheme to save money at major supermarkets, retailers, gyms, restaurants, insurance providers and many more. Health Cash Plan. Fantastic development opportunities to learn and progress. Further details can be found on the benefits section of our website . Job summary The Digital Project Manager is responsible for leading the delivery of digital, data and technology related projects across the ICO. Reporting to the Digital Programme Manager, the Digital Project Manager ensures that projects are delivered effectively, consistently, and with measurable impact. The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) is the independent regulator of information rights. In a data-driven world, we provide advice, guidance, and support to organisations enabling compliance with their obligations, as well as protecting individuals and their personal data. As an employer, we are passionate about making a positive difference to the lives and careers of our people, and we empower you to be curious, impactful, collaborative and respectful. Job description This role requires proactivity and versatility to manage delivery across the organisation, support the embedding of change and contribute to the continuous improvement of delivery practice. The Digital Project Manager will work with and empower project teams, scrum teams, manage interdependencies and risks, and ensure that delivery is aligned with organisational priorities and to governance standards. Key responsibilities: Lead the delivery of DDaT projects in alignment with organisational priorities whilst ensuring projects teams are empowered to deliver effectively. Use skills and experience to lead and direct end-to-end project delivery, working closely with roles within the digital delivery team such as Scrum Masters, User Centre Design specialists, Technical Business Analysts , Test Engineers , Product Owners and Architecture. Develop and maintain a comprehensive approach to project delivery by use of the Agile methods in a JIRA environment. Identify and proactively manage cross-organisational resource required to successfully delivery projects. Lead on the engagement with and coordination of actions across stakeholder groups within wider business. Ensure effective assurance reporting and visibility of deliverables, risks, and issues by monitoring and controlling project progress using appropriate tools, and by preparing and delivering reports and papers for project and programme boards. Where appropriate, provide leadership, coaching, challenge and guidance to ensure objectives are met and delivery is consistent across the organisation. Ensure outputs are effectively implemented and embedded within the business. Provide business process change support, coordinate communications and training activities, and work in partnership with stakeholders and benefit owners to maximise adoption and realise benefits. Facilitate lessons learned exercises, embedding findings into delivery practice to support a continuous learning culture and improve project management standards. Organise and support project events, including workshops, stakeholder briefings, and assurance activities. Person specification Essential criteria assessed at application stage: Experience of managing and delivering projects in public or private sector environments. Evidence of successful implementation of projects that deliver strategic value across varied domains including but not limited to digital, data, regulatory, and transformational workstreams Very strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to negotiate and to build and maintain good working relationships both internally and externally, up to and including senior management level. Excellent understanding and application of Agile delivery methodologies including Scrum . Good working knowledge of JIRA . Ability to deliver projects under strategic oversight, working in partnership with the Digital Programme Manager to ensure alignment with organisational priorities. Demonstrated leadership in managing project teams, with experience in coaching, mentoring, and developing capability across a matrix environment. Understanding of portfolio, programme and project governance and assurance, with the ability to contribute to reporting and decision-making processes. Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the ability to represent project interests across governance forums and enable effective decision-making . Excellent judgement and the ability to deal with a changing environment both on a day-to-day and long-term basis. Commitment to continuous improvement, with experience in leading lessons learned exercises and embedding findings into delivery practice. Essential criteria assessed during interview: Experience of managing and delivering projects in public or private sector environments. Evidence of successful implementation of projects that deliver strategic value across varied domains including but not limited to digital, data, regulatory, and transformational workstreams Very strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to negotiate and to build and maintain good working relationships both internally and externally, up to and including senior management level. Good working knowledge of JIRA and the application of Agile Scrum. Ability to deliver projects under strategic oversight, working in partnership with the Digital Programme Manager to ensure alignment with organisational priorities. Understanding of portfolio, programme and project governance and assurance, with the ability to contribute to reporting and decision-making processes. Excellent judgement and the ability to deal with a changing environment both on a day-to-day and long-term basis. Commitment to continuous improvement, with experience in leading lessons learned exercises and embedding findings into delivery practice. Equality, diversity, and inclusion The ICO is committed to promoting and enhancing equality, diversity, and inclusion. We are focused on developing a workforce that is representative of the communities we serve and together we are building an inclusive workplace where all of our colleagues have the opportunity to make a real difference. We are championing this through our Equality Diversity and Inclusion Board together with a number of staff networks. Read more about our commitment on our website. Candidates with a disability who meet the minimum criteria for this vacancy will be invited to interview as part of the ICO’s commitment to the Disability Confident Scheme. As part of the ICO’s commitment to our EDI objectives and creating a workplace that represents the communities and societies we serve, we guarantee an interview to candidates who declare they identify as belonging from an ethnic minority background and who meet the minimum criteria for this vacancy If you are disabled or have an impairment and require an alternative application method, please email the HR team at recruitment@ico.org.uk Closing Date Please submit your CV and cover letter by 23:59, Thursday 17 September Your cover letter should be no more than 1,000 words and should clearly demonstrate how you meet the essential criteria for the role. We may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. To ensure your application is considered, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support your application, please contact us at recruitment@ico.org.uk . I n the event of a high volume of applications, we may not be able to invite all candidates who meet the minimum criteria to interview. However, we encourage you stay in touch and apply for future roles that match your interests. All candidates who meet the minimum criteria and apply in-line with our guaranteed interview scheme for disabled and ethnic minority applicants will be interviewed. Clearance Required for this role: Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS)
